guidance_for_write_dockerfile_agent: The Dockerfile build fails at the step: 'RUN python3.11 -m ensurepip --upgrade && python3.11 -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel'. The error message is: 'ensurepip is disabled in Debian/Ubuntu for the system python. Python modules for the system python are usually handled by dpkg and apt-get. Install the python3-pip package to use pip itself. Using pip together with the system python might have unexpected results for any system installed module, so use it on your own risk, or make sure to only use it in virtual environments.' This indicates that calling 'python3.11 -m ensurepip' on Ubuntu 22.04 system python is disabled, causing the failure. To fix this, you should replace the 'ensurepip' step by directly installing 'python3-pip' via apt-get, and then use 'pip3' for upgrading pip, setuptools, and wheel. Alternatively, you can avoid installing pip globally and only set up the virtual environment, then install pip and dependencies inside it. For example, add 'apt-get install -y python3-pip' before any pip commands, and modify the pip upgrade commands to 'pip3 install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel'. This will ensure that pip is available and upgradeable on the system and inside virtual environment. Avoid calling 'ensurepip' on system python on Ubuntu since it is disabled. Also confirm the virtual environment uses the correct python3.11 interpreter and pip.
